title: Snowsports School Cancellation Terms: Notice, What Is Retained and What Comes Back
content:
A household may give a Snowsports School booking up at any time, and what they get back turns on how much notice they gave.

## 1. The free cancellation deadline

A cancellation carries no fee only when it is recorded on or before the free cancellation deadline, which is the product's free cancellation period measured back from the moment the first session is due to start.

The notice period is measured in whole elapsed hours on the mountain's local clock and is subtracted from the scheduled start of the first session to give the deadline; elapsed hours are never mixed with calendar days, and an hour begun is not an hour elapsed. The moment the first session is due to start is read from the booking record itself — the date the first session is due to run and the scheduled start on that date — matched to the cancellation by the booking reference. A cancellation recorded at the deadline itself is on the free side of it.

## 2. What comes back

Inside that deadline the whole tuition raised for the booking comes back and any add-ons come back with it.

After it, the product's late cancellation share of the booking price is retained as a fee and the remainder comes back.

Where sessions have already been delivered, only the sessions still to come are given back, worked out as the tuition divided by the sessions the block held and multiplied by the sessions still to come.

## 3. Sessions the collective cannot run

The following clause is **no longer in force**: "Where the collective cancels the session for weather, mountain conditions or an instructor being unavailable, the product's weather basis decides what the household receives and no fee is retained." It is carried here only so that no reader applies it, the current basis for a session lost to the mountain having replaced it.

## 4. The form what comes back takes

What comes back is issued as school credit; a return to the original payment method is a finance team decision rather than a desk decision.

## 5. Boundary readings of the deadline

Take a booking of a product whose free cancellation period is 48 hours, whose first session is due to start at 09:30 on a stated date. The deadline falls at 09:30 two days earlier.

| Moment the cancellation is recorded | Reading |
| --- | --- |
| 09:00 on the deadline day | 48 whole hours have not yet elapsed towards the start, so the cancellation is inside the free period |
| 09:30 on the deadline day, exactly at the deadline | on the deadline, and so still free of fee |
| 09:31 on the deadline day | the deadline has passed, and the late cancellation share is retained |
| the morning of the session day | the deadline has long passed, and the late cancellation share is retained |

## 6. Reading of the sessions still to come

Take a hypothetical booking whose block held 5 sessions and on which 2 sessions have already been delivered, on which tuition of 2000.00 USD stands, and whose product retains a late cancellation share of 40.00 percent. The tuition divided by the 5 sessions the block held is 400.00 USD a session; multiplied by the 3 sessions still to come it is 1200.00 USD; the late cancellation share retained on that figure is 480.00 USD, so 720.00 USD comes back, rounded to the cent. Where the reckoning would fall below nothing, nothing comes back.

The free cancellation periods, late cancellation shares, session counts and refund processing times these terms turn on are published product by product on the Snowsports School tariff.
